messages:
maya: heads up — us-west1 GPU fleet is in an eviction loop, lots of tiny leftover GPUs (1/8 fractional alloc) and pods bouncing. seeing spike in 10:30 UTC. :(

maya: top symptoms — high pod Pending with 'insufficient nvidia.com/gpu', but nodes show free GPU fragments spread across many nodes. also net-attach plugin delays reported in the same window.

diego: ugh that sounds like binpacking+startup latency combo. are these new model jobs with fractional GPU requests?

maya: yes, most are 0.125 or 0.25 GPU requests (we're running multi-tenant inference workers). scheduler is scattering them to avoid >1 gpu per node but we want to pack.

sam: quick q — is the scheduler using our custom Score plugin for packing? or default binpack?

maya: still using default PackingPriority with our label scoring, but looks like topologySpread is kicking in (we force AZ spread). combination -> tiny slices everywhere.

anika: also saw k8s events about network-setup timeout during CNI init. some pods failing liveness probe because of delayed eth0 up. that triggers eviction/backoff which leaves 0.125 GPUs stranded on nodes.

sam: ok so two levers: 1) avoid spreading for these tiny jobs (allow binpack), 2) reduce eviction on transient net failures (tolerate short network delays).

diego: agreed. proposal: create a new schedClass label on podspecs: scheduling.k8s.io/pack=compact for fractional-gpu workloads. add a Priority/Score tweak to prefer nodes with existing pack pods. also set podTopologySpread constraint to prefer not required.

maya: +1. what about immediate mitigations? can we run a descheduler job to consolidate fragments?

anika: we have a descheduler job but it's off in prod (risky with stateful infra). we could run a dry-run first and then full on a single AZ.

sam: for the eviction loop, we should increase kubelet's eviction grace for network-unavailable conditions. current config evicts at 30s. bump to 2m for this class via pod annotation and node-level threshold? kubelet doesn't support per-pod grace — but we can add tolerations for the net-ready taint and set startupProbe to be longer.

maya: example startupProbe change we used before:
```
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  failureThreshold: 12  # ~120s with periodSeconds 10
  periodSeconds: 10
```

diego: also add toleration for taint node.kubernetes.io/network-unavailable:NoExecute with tolerationSeconds=180 so short net hiccups don't evict.

sam: putting this together: 1) rollout schedClass label and scoring change (staged canary), 2) create a temporary Descheduler job in us-west1-a, run in dry-run then reconcile, 3) patch pod templates to add startupProbe + toleration for fractional workloads, 4) investigate CNI daemonset logs (calico/flannel) for long DHCP/mtu delays.

anika: i'll take CNI logs. initial grep shows flannel restarts on 3 nodes around 10:28 UTC (kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/flannel | grep "error" --since=15m). sending raw logs to #eng-infra.

maya: we also need cost angle — packing into fewer nodes is cheaper (GPU utilization up) but pushes thermal/IO on those nodes; ops wants to ensure we don't overload GPU SM or host NIC. any telemetry we should monitor?

diego: monitor token: gpu_utilization, host_cpu, host_gpu_mem, nic_tx_errors, pod_network_latency. add an SLO alert if any of those exceed 85% sustained for 2m during consolidation.

sam: action items:
- diego: PR to scheduler scoring plugin (prefer nodes with label pack=compact) and a canary job.
- anika: collect and post CNI logs + reconcile flannel restarts.
- maya: schedule descheduler dry-run in us-west1-a (low-traffic window 02:00 PDT).
- sam: create k8s patch template for startupProbe + toleration + annot pack.

anika: note — we should also consider adding a periodic "fragmentation_report" metric exported by node-exporter: percent_gpus_unused_fragments and smallest_free_fragment_size. will help detect regression.

diego: love that. I'll add a prometheus rule and dashboard tile.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook link added: https://runbook.internal/redwood/gpu-fragmentation with steps for triage and rollback. :robot_face:

maya: thanks all. i'll start the descheduler dry-run in 20m and loop back.

sam: FYI — if descheduler makes large moves, we should use PodDisruptionBudget for stateful-ish infra. otherwise expect a short spike in restarts.

maya: noted. will add PDBs for critical services.

diego: ping once dry-run results are in. if packing yields >20% reduction in nodes used without >10% increase in per-node gpu_temp or net errors, we can roll to other AZs.

maya: dry-run done — results: reclaimed ~18 GPU slices into 3 nodes, nodes used down 12%, no CPU/gpu temp uptick immediately. posting dry-run diff below.

maya: ```
Descheduler dry-run summary:
- fragments before: 47 nodes with <0.5 free GPU
- fragments after (simulated): 29 nodes with <0.5 free GPU
- pods rescheduled (simulated): 82 fractional pods
- predicted free nodes reclaimed: 3
```

anika: good. next step: run actual job in a single AZ during midnight window and monitor. I'll tail the CNI logs and prometheus dashboards.

sam: leaving notes for canary PRs. thanks team :thumbsup:

sre-bot: alert suppressed for us-west1 GPU pending count during maintenance window (1887654300 - 1887655300).
